1  THIS MFA FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 20.11.2020 PASSED IN MVC NO. 1699/2018 ON THE FILE OF THE ADDITIONAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE, MACT, SRIRANGAPATNA,
PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE DR. JUSTICE CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA  ORAL JUDGMENT Heard Sri.Srinivas.V, learned counsel for the appellant as well as Sri.Sunil Kumar.

K, learned counsel who represents Sri.H.S.Lingaraju, learned counsel on record for respondent No.2.
2.
This is a claimant's appeal.
Challenge in this appeal is the order that is rendered by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Srirangapatna in MVC No.1699/2018 dated 20.11.2020.
On the ground that she sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident and became permanently disabled, the appellant claimed compensation of Rs.33,50,000/- in total.
The Tribunal through the impugned order awarded a sum of Rs.6,68,298/- as NC: 2024:KHC:37144 compensation.
Dissatisfied with the same, the claimant is before this Court.
3. Arguing the matter, learned counsel Sri.Srinivas.V, for the appellant submits that the appellant sustained grievous head injury which resulted in permanent physical disability.
Learned counsel contends that the appellant as a home maker was attending her duties, but due to the injuries sustained she is unable to do any work.
Though Cw.1 deposed with regard to the nature of injury sustained and the disability, the Tribunal took the disability in respect of whole body as 22% which is erroneous.
Learned counsel thereby seeks for enhancement of compensation.

4. The submission that is made by Sri.Sunil Kumar.K for respondent No.2 on the other hand is that the Tribunal taking into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case awarded justifiable sum as compensation and therefore, the award needs no interference.

Subjecting the evidence of Pw.1, Cw.1, Ex.P5 to Ex.P13 and Ex.C1 to Ex.C14 to scrutiny, the Tribunal came to a conclusion that the sum that is liable to be awarded as compensation is Rs.6,68,298/-.
6.

The Tribunal awarded the said sum divided under following heads:

4 Loss of income during  Rs.15,000  treatment period
5 Loss of income towards  Rs.2,57,400  permanent disability  6 Disappointment and  discomfort and loss of Rs.20,000  amenities  Total Rs.6,68,298 7.

By the evidence of Cw.1, it is clear that apart from hemorrhagic contusions at left fronto temporal NC: 2024:KHC:37144 regions and bilateral parietal lobes, the appellant sustained multiple fractures of skull.
He also deposed that the appellant underwent right temporo parietal craniotomy and evacuation of ESDH.
She also underwent tracheostomy.
Cw.1 stated that the disability is 65%.
However, considering the totality of evidence, the Tribunal took the disability in respect of whole body as 22% which needs no interference.
8. Having considered the absence of any proof with regard to the occupation and earnings of the appellant, the Tribunal took the notional income as Rs.7,500/- which also needs no interference.

However, this Court is of the view that the compensation awarded under the head pain and suffering i.e., Rs.40,000/- is grossly low in the light of the grievous injuries sustained by the appellant and surgeries she underwent.
Also having considered the nature of injuries sustained, this Court is of the view that the appellant would not have attended her normal pursuits at least for a period of six months.
However, the Tribunal did not award any amount towards attendant charges.
Also the amount awarded under the head loss of amenities i.e., Rs.20,000/- is grossly low.
Therefore, this Court is of the considered view that the sum which is required to be awarded in addition to the sum that is awarded by the Tribunal under all those heads is Rs.1,00,000/-.
Thus this Court considers desirable to enhance the compensation by Rs.1,00,000/-.

Therefore, the appeal Smt Mangalagowramma @ Mangalagowri vs Sri Rajegowda on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31734589/
3 is disposed of with the following:

NC: 2024:KHC:37144 (iv) Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the enhanced sum within a period of 8(eight) weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
